top_choice_rationale: Optical lattice clocks for Katori and Ye are a distinct, identifiable invention (the magic-wavelength lattice) with an identifiable origin and an uncontested two-name credit. The scheme has been reproduced at roughly 1e-18 in several independent laboratories and already yields redshift and varying-constant tests. The overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes can be handled by a citation naming the lattice scheme. P002 is a close second: a conceptually important, mature Z2 classification, but its credit is incomplete (Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang, Hasan) and it sits next to the 2016 prize. An award is preferable to no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile for P001 or P002; my TEM background is professionally close to B039, which is not on the slate, and Goran Johansson is a Chalmers colleague, relevant only to circuit QED, which is not on the slate
